written.myAnswer: A distance–time graph shows how an object's distance changes with time. A speed–time graph shows how its speed changes with time.

For a time interval Δt, the distance covered is speed × time, so it equals the area of the strip under the speed–time graph (height v and width Δt). Adding these strips over the whole journey gives total distance = area under the graph. For example, if speed changes uniformly from u to v in time t, distance = average speed × time = [(u + v)/2]t, which is the area of the trapezium under the graph.
